author: Brenton Kemp
title: Logan Henderson (back) to start Thursday versus Cardinals
desc: Brewers right-hander Logan Henderson (back) will be activated from the injured list to start Thursday's game against the Cardinals.
impact: It was reported that Henderson would make a start for the Brewers at some point this week, and it will indeed come as part of a rare five-game set against the Cardinals on Thursday. The right-hander has been on the injured list since May 26 with a low back strain and posted a 2.74 ERA across five starts prior to hitting the shelf.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Roman Anthony (finger) to see specialist Wednesday
desc: Red Sox outfielder Roman Anthony (finger) will meet with hand specialist Dr. Gary Lourie in Atlanta on Wednesday.
impact: It was reported that Anthony would visit a specialist this week, and that will take place in Atlanta on Wednesday with Dr. Gary Lourie. Given Anthony's limited progress since being placed on the injured list in May 7, the visit is to gauge how the healing is going. Anthony won't be available to the club until August, at the earliest, while Wednesday's visit could result in a different course of action. Stay tuned.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Connelly Early (elbow) will get second opinion Thursday
desc: Red Sox left-hander Connelly Early (elbow) will see Dr. Keith Meister on Thursday for a second opinion after an MRI revealed he has posterior elbow inflammation.
impact: Red Sox manager Chad Tracy had said Early will seek a second opinion on his elbow, as most do with arm injuries, and that is set to take place on Thursday with renowned elbow specialist Dr. Keith Meister. Early has been on the injured list since July 1 and posted a 3.44 ERA across 17 starts prior to hitting the shelf.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Yimi Garcia (elbow) to throw bullpen session this week
desc: Blue Jays reliever Yimi Garcia (elbow) is expected to get on the mound and throw a bullpen session this week.
impact: Garcia had a setback and recently resumed throwing as he continues to claw his way back from 2025 right elbow surgery. The veteran is hoping to get on a mound for a bullpen this week and begin to build up again. His late-July timetable seems optimistic at this point.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Henry Bolte homers in loss to Tigers
desc: Henry Bolte went 1-for-3 in a loss to the Tigers with a home run, two runs scored, one RBI, and one walk.
impact: Bolte continues a impactful stretch of late, getting on base in nine of his last 12 contests. The outfielder has offered. manager Mark Kotsay one of the more reliable bats in an inconsistent Athletics lineup, batting .292 with three home runs, 15 RBI, 18 runs scored, and 11 stolen bases across 49 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Ben Rice drives in three in loss to Rays
desc: Ben Rice went 3-for-4 in Tuesday's loss to the Rays with a home run, one run scored, and three RBI.
impact: Rice has heated back up of late, getting on base in each of his last seven contests. The first baseman continues to reward manager Aaron Boone as one of the more explosive bats in a Yankees lineup missing Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton, carrying a .941 OPS with 26 home runs, 60 RBI, 60 runs scored, and two stolen bases across 86 games.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Andrew Abbott takes loss Tuesday versus Phillies
desc: Reds left-hander Andrew Abbott surrendered three earned runs on five hits across six innings, taking the loss against the Phillies on Tuesday.
impact: Despite tossing a quality start, Abbott was hit with his fifth loss of the season as his counterpart, Phillies right-hander Zack Wheeler, stole the show with seven innings of one-run ball with a whopping 14 strikeouts to eliminate any chance of Abbott avoiding the loss. The southpaw has been a model of consistency for the Reds for quite some time, allowing three earned runs or fewer while going at least five innings in 13 consecutive starts dating back to April 30. He will carry a 3.92 ERA into his next scheduled start, which lines up as the Reds' final contest before the All-Star Game, at home against the Cubs on Sunday.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Eugenio Suarez swats homer in loss to Phillies Tuesday
desc: Reds third baseman Eugenio Suarez went 1-for-4 with a solo homer in a 4-1 loss to the Phillies on Tuesday.
impact: Suarez's seventh-inning solo homer, his ninth of the season, provided the lone offense of the evening for the Reds, as they were dominated by Phillies right-hander Zack Wheeler to the tune of one earned run on four hits to go along with 14 strikeouts across seven innings. Despite the long ball, it's been a vastly disappointing season at the plate for Suarez, who is slashing just .207/.280/.374 with nine homers, 21 runs, 32 RBI, and a 75 wRC+ that represents production 25% below the league average.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Will Warren shelled in loss to Rays
desc: Will Warren allowed six earned runs on seven hits and two walks while striking out three over four innings in Tuesday's loss to the Rays.
impact: Warren has offered mixed results on the mound of late, allowing three earned runs or more in three of his last six contests. The right-hander remains one of the more inconsistent arms in the Yankees rotation to this point, posting a 4.15 ERA and 1.37 WHIP with a 7-4 record and 9.1 K/9 ratio across 18 starts.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Patrick Corbin picks up win over Giants Tuesday
desc: Blue Jays left-hander Patrick Corbin pitched 2 1/3 innings, allowing one earned run on two hits while picking up the win over the Giants on Tuesday.
impact: Corbin followed right-hander Spencer Miles in this one and walked into a win as Miles left the game after four innings with the Jays leading 8-2. Corbin covered more than enough ground to quality for the win as he struck out two and didn't walk a batter in his outing. The veteran is currently pitching out of the bullpen after some struggles following a solid start to the season in the team's rotation, and sports a 5.07 ERA across 17 outings (15 starts) this season.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Spencer Miles takes no-decision in win over Giants Tuesday
desc: Blue Jays right-hander Spencer Miles pitched four innings, allowing two runs on seven hits in a no-decision against the Giants on Tuesday.
impact: Miles wasn't great in this one, allowing a pair of earned runs on seven hits in four innings of work, but he also didn't walk a batter. He struck out one. The good news is the Blue Jays' offensive finally figured it out at the plate, plating eight runs before Miles departed the contest after four innings in an eventual 9-3 victory. The right-hander never figured to get deep into this one, as his four innings came just one out shy of tying his season-high in innings pitched this season. It's unclear when the Jays will turn to Miles again, as he owns an excellent 2.95 ERA across 25 appearances (three starts) and 58 innings pitched this season.

author: Nate Miller
title: Connor Thomas sent down to minors
desc: Connor Thomas was optioned back to Triple-A on Wednesday.
impact: It was a short stint in the Braves' bullpen for Thomas, as he was just called up on Tuesday. The 28-year-old lefty worked 3 2/3 innings out of the Braves' pen in Tuesday's loss, giving up four earned runs on five hits and a walk. Victor Mederos was recalled in a corresponding move.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Ernie Clement collects three knocks in win over Giants Tuesday
desc: Blue Jays second baseman Ernie Clement went 3-for-4 with a run scored and an RBI in a 9-3 win over the Giants on Tuesday.
impact: The Blue Jays finally erupted at the plate on Tuesday, as Clement accounted for three of 13 Blue Jays hits on the evening. The All-Star singled twice and doubled, recording a sac fly in the third before scoring the game's final run on an RBI groundout in the ninth. The 30-year-old has been quiet while dealing with a hip issue of late, as Clement had just two hits in his previous four games prior to leading the charge on Tuesday. He is slashing .298/.319/.434 with seven homers, 38 runs, 30 RBI, and a pair of stolen bases across 89 games this season.

author: Nate Miller
title: Victor Mederos recalled from Triple-A
desc: Victor Mederos was called up from Triple-A Gwinnett on Wednesday.
impact: Mederos will join the Braves for the second time this season. The righty made an appearance back on May 20, tossing two scoreless innings against the Marlins. Connor Thomas was optioned to Triple-A in a corresponding move.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Jonatan Clase hits homer in win over Giants Tuesday
desc: Blue Jays outfielder Jonatan Clase went 2-for-4 with a three-run homer and an additional run scored in a 9-3 win over the Giants on Tuesday.
impact: Perhaps the Blue Jays have the youngtser to thank for their offensive eruption following a series of pitiful games at the plate, as the 24-year-old blasted a three-run homer to get the scoring started in the top of the second inning on Tuesday. It was Clase's first start since being brought to the big leagues on June 4, as he also singled and scored in the third inning. The rookie hit just .223 with five homers, 17 stolen bases, and a .680 OPS in 53 games with Triple-A Buffalo prior to his promotion, so an offensive surge in the big leagues is unlikely moving forward.
